title: Dionysus — Variants across tellings
summary: Dionysus is god of wine, theater, and ecstatic ritual. This study compares how different sources tell the tale.
body:
Dionysus is god of wine, theater, and ecstatic ritual. His worship could dissolve social order, as in Euripides's Bacchae.

No myth has one true version. Dionysus survives in competing tellings — poets, priests, and painters each shaping it to their purpose. The variants disagree, and the disagreements are themselves revealing. Viewed through a symbolic lens, Dionysus is read for its images — what each figure and object stands for beneath the plot.

The 'real' Dionysus is the whole cloud of versions, not any single text. One fruitful sub-question is which telling of Dionysus is oldest, and how the tale changed in transmission. Related entries in this archive: Achilles and Trojan War.
